title: The Drop of Honey (हिन्दी)

full_text:
In a bustling marketplace of Baghdad, a confectioner was filling a clay jar with golden wild honey. Through a moment of careless haste, a single sweet drop of honey dripped from his wooden ladle onto the doorstep.

A green fly smelled the sweetness and landed on the drop to feed.

A lizard darted out from a crack in the brick wall and snatched the fly with its tongue.

The confectioner’s pet cat leaped from the counter and pounced upon the lizard, crushing it beneath its claws.

At that moment, the neighbor’s hunting hound saw the cat, surged forward with a furious bark, and seized the cat by the neck.

The confectioner, seeing his beloved cat attacked, seized a heavy rolling pin and struck the hound.

The owner of the hound, a fierce butcher from across the alley, saw his dog struck, seized his meat cleaver, and rushed at the confectioner.

The sweetmakers of the bazaar rushed to defend the confectioner, while the butchers rallied to support their companion! Sticks, knives, and stones were thrown, and within an hour, half the market was in flames, stalls were plundered, and thirty citizens were bruised and wounded before the city watch arrived to restore order!

The Chief Judge sat in the public square, surveying the smoking ruins of the bazaar, and asked: 'What great feud ignited this terrible catastrophe?'

The trembling confectioner stepped forward, bowed his head in tears, and confessed: 'It was nothing, my lord... it was only a single drop of honey that fell upon the doorstep!'

The judge sighed with deep philosophical sorrow: 'Behold how a tiny spark of carelessness, fed by hasty wrath, burns an entire city to ashes! He who cannot control his temper over a drop of honey is not worthy to walk among civilized men.'
moral: Small negligences and petty disputes, if not checked with patience, spiral into catastrophic ruin. [HI]
